targets.target: 0A: relative effective Cartier divisors on smooth relative curves, with fibre criterion, sections, sums, degree, incidence loci and the subgroup criterion
targets.note: No effective Cartier divisor exists in either library; only generic inputs (finite ⇔ proper and quasi-finite, locally constant rank) are present. Details under 0A.

targets.target: 0B: finite locally free commutative group schemes, kernels, fppf quotients, constant and diagonalizable groups, Cartier duality, (ℤ/N)ᴰ ≅ μ_N, killing by the rank
targets.note: Over an affine base Tau Ceti has Cartier duality with biduality and base change, constant groups, μ_n = D(ℤ/n), kernels and fppf quotient sheaves. Missing: the non-affine base, representability of quotients, exactness, the duality (ℤ/N)ᴰ ≅ μ_N and Deligne's theorem. Details under 0B.

targets.target: 0C: affine quotients by finite groups, finite group-scheme torsors, SGA 3 V 4.1 quotients by finite locally free equivalence relations
targets.note: Only integrality over the invariant ring (and, by composition, module-finiteness under finite type) is available; no scheme quotients. Details under 0C.

targets.target: 0D: finite étale schemes, and finite étale K-schemes ≃ finite continuous Galois sets with transport of group objects and pairings
targets.note: Étale cancellation and the separably closed case exist; the Galois-set equivalence over a general field does not. Details under 0D.

targets.target: 0E: effective fppf descent for the listed objects, and spreading out
targets.note: Descent of morphisms (subcanonical fpqc and fppf topologies) and spreading out of morphisms exist; effective descent of objects does not. Details under 0E.

targets.target: 0F: Weil restriction along finite locally free maps and the Hom-schemes it represents
targets.note: Details under 0F.

targets.target: 0G: the relative Grassmannian and the parameter scheme of rank-N subgroup schemes
targets.note: Only the Grassmannian functor; representability is a Mathlib TODO. Details under 0G.

duplicates.note: Owns étale equivalence-relation quotients and effective descent for sheaves, finite flat groups, polarisations and projective objects: most of 0C and 0E in general form.
Owns Cartier duality and finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions, the general theory behind 0B.

targets.target: Relative effective Cartier divisor on C/S: an effective Cartier divisor whose closed subscheme is flat over S (one shared carrier)
targets.note: Tau Ceti's CartierDivisor is the group of global sections of 𝒦ˣ/𝒪ˣ on an integral scheme: absolute, not effective, and with no flatness over a base. Mathlib has ideal sheaves and closed subschemes but no invertible-ideal (effective Cartier) predicate, relative or absolute. The phrase 'relative effective Cartier divisor' occurs only in Tau Ceti comments that cite the Jacobian Challenge roadmap.

targets.target: Fibre criterion: over a locally noetherian S, with C/S flat and locally of finite type and D ⊆ C closed, finitely presented and S-flat, D is relative effective Cartier iff every geometric fibre is; plus the limit/descent version
targets.note: Neither library has the local criterion for flatness, regular sequences along fibres, or any fibrewise test for invertibility of an ideal sheaf.

targets.target: A section P : S ⟶ C of a separated smooth relative curve defines the relative effective Cartier divisor [P]
targets.note: Only the closed-image half exists: if f ≫ g is a closed immersion and g is separated then f is a closed immersion, so a section of a separated morphism is a closed immersion. Missing: that its ideal sheaf is invertible and that the resulting divisor is S-flat of degree one.

targets.target: Sums, inverse images under flat morphisms, and arbitrary base change preserve relative effective Cartier divisors
targets.note: No carrier, so none of the stability statements exists.

targets.target: A relative effective Cartier divisor is finite over S iff proper over S, and is then finite locally free
targets.note: Mathlib proves finite ⇔ proper and locally quasi-finite for any morphism (Stacks 02LS). Missing: quasi-finiteness of a relative Cartier divisor on a curve, and the conclusion that it is finite locally free.

targets.target: Degree of a divisor as the locally constant rank of a finite locally free morphism; inverse images under finite flat maps of curves multiply degrees
targets.note: The rank function of a finite flat morphism, its local constancy under local finite presentation, and its invariance under base change are in Mathlib. There is no degree of a divisor, and no multiplicativity of finrank along a composite of finite flat morphisms (FlatRank.lean has only composition with an isomorphism).

targets.target: Universal incidence locus D′ ≤ D and equality locus D′ = D: scheme structures, universal properties, base change
targets.note: No representability result for containment or equality of closed subschemes exists in either library.

targets.target: Subgroup criterion for a finite locally free divisor on a commutative smooth relative curve, in terms of identity, inversion and addition
targets.note: No group-scheme statement about divisors exists. Tau Ceti's ClosedSubgroupScheme is only a closed-immersion subobject of a group object.

duplicates.note: Lists relative effective Cartier divisors as its own target; 0A says to use that shared definition and adds only the KM-specific lemmas.
Also proves that a section through the smooth locus of a relative curve is an effective Cartier divisor, that sums of disjoint sections are, and that both commute with base change (0A items 2–3).

targets.target: Affine group schemes over Spec R anti-equivalent to commutative Hopf algebras (consumed from Group/Affine.lean)
targets.note: Mathlib has hopfSpec fully faithful with affine group schemes as essential image, as the roadmap says. Tau Ceti assembles these into the equivalence (CommHopfAlgCat R)ᵒᵖ ≌ AffineGroupSchemeCat.

targets.target: The category of finite locally free (finite, flat, locally finitely presented) commutative group schemes over S
targets.note: Exists over an affine base Spec R, with finiteness, flatness, local finite presentation and commutativity all built in. Missing: the category over an arbitrary base scheme S, which the roadmap uses throughout.

targets.target: Scheme-theoretic kernel of an arbitrary homomorphism, with base change (and no claim that it is finite locally free)
targets.note: For a morphism of affine group schemes over Spec R: the kernel as the closed subgroup cut out by the kernel Hopf ideal, the pullback square against the identity section, and the coordinate ring K ⊗_H R. Missing: kernels of homomorphisms of non-affine group schemes over a general base (such as E ⟶ E′) and a stated base-change theorem for them.

targets.target: fppf quotient G/C by a closed finite locally free subgroup, representable under 0C's hypotheses, with G ⟶ G/C an fppf-exact sequence
targets.note: Over an affine base Tau Ceti builds the fppf quotient sheaf of an affine group by a closed normal subgroup, with its universal property, local surjectivity of the projection and the torsor kernel pair. It asserts no representability. Missing: a scheme representing G/C, and exactness over a non-affine base.

targets.target: Constant finite group scheme G_S = ⨆_{g∈G} S ≅ Spec ∏ 𝒪_S, coordinate algebra Map(G,R) over Spec R
targets.note: Over Spec R for a finite group G: the constant group scheme with coordinate ring identified with G → R, finite and étale. The coproduct description ⨆ S and the version over a non-affine base are not stated.

targets.target: Diagonalizable group scheme D_S(M) = Spec 𝒪_S[M], and μ_N = D_S(ℤ/N)
targets.note: Over Spec R: D(M) for a finitely generated abelian group M, μ_n = D(ℤ/n) with points the n-th roots of unity, and μ_n as the kernel of the n-th power map of 𝔾ₘ on points. The roadmap's base is an arbitrary scheme; over an affine base the target is met.

targets.target: Cartier duality as an anti-equivalence on finite locally free commutative group schemes, with evaluation, biduality, rank and base change
targets.note: Complete over an affine base Spec R: the anti-equivalence, natural biduality G ≅ D(D(G)), and compatibility with base change along R ⟶ S. The index drops the TauCeti. prefix of these names. Missing: Cartier duality over a non-affine base, preservation of rank, and the evaluation pairing G × Gᴰ ⟶ 𝔾ₘ as a named morphism.

targets.target: Exactness of Cartier duality on fppf-exact sequences of finite locally free groups; kernel–quotient comparison
targets.note: No short exact sequence of finite flat group schemes, and no exactness statement for duality, exists in either library.

targets.target: ((ℤ/N)_S)ᴰ ≅ μ_N and (μ_N)ᴰ ≅ (ℤ/N)_S
targets.note: Both sides exist over Spec R, and the constant group's coordinate ring is even defined as the finite dual of the group algebra R[G], but no isomorphism between the Cartier dual of one and the other is stated.

targets.target: A finite locally free commutative group scheme of rank N is killed by N (Deligne)
targets.note: Not in either library under any name; no statement about multiplication by the rank on a finite flat group scheme exists.

duplicates.note: Develops Cartier duality, finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions and fpqc descent for finite flat group schemes, the general theory 0B specialises.
Owns D(M) and μ_n = D(ℤ/n), and names Cartier duality of finite locally free commutative group schemes as a separate target; Tau Ceti's affine-base Cartier duality was built against this layer.
Owns kernels and the fppf sheaf quotient G/H with representability as a separate theorem, which is where Tau Ceti's kernelSpec and fppfQuotientSheaf were built.

targets.target: Affine quotient Spec A^G by a finite group acting on Spec A, with its categorical universal property among schemes
targets.note: Mathlib has the invariant subalgebra, but no scheme-level quotient by a group action and no universal property of Spec A^G.

targets.target: A is integral over A^G
targets.note: For a finite group G acting on B and any A ⟶ B whose image contains the fixed points, B is integral over A. Taking A = A^G gives the target.

targets.target: If A is of finite type over an invariant base ring and G acts by base-algebra automorphisms, A is module-finite over A^G, so the quotient map is finite
targets.note: Not stated, but it is a three-step composition in Mathlib: integrality over A^G (above), finite type over A^G by the tower lemma, and integral plus finite type gives module-finite. Tau Ceti proves only the case of a group algebra over a Galois extension of fields.

targets.target: Finite locally free group-scheme torsors on affine schemes: Hopf–Galois criterion, invariant algebra, faithful flatness, descent, affine fppf quotient with universal property
targets.note: No Hopf–Galois extension or comodule-algebra torsor exists. The Tau Ceti torsor square concerns an affine group modulo a closed normal subgroup, not a group scheme acting on an arbitrary affine scheme.

targets.target: SGA 3 V 4.1, affine case: a finite locally free equivalence relation R ⇉ X on affine X has an affine quotient X/R, X ⟶ X/R finite locally free surjective, R = X ×_{X/R} X, representing the fppf quotient sheaf
targets.note: No quotient by an equivalence relation in schemes exists. Mathlib only has Zariski-local representability of a sheaf covered by relatively representable open immersions, which is the gluing input.

targets.target: Free action of a finite constant group with an invariant affine open cover: glue the affine invariant quotients and represent the fppf quotient; check the hypothesis for the moduli schemes of Layers 4, 5 and 9
targets.note: Nothing about free group actions on schemes or their quotients exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Owns finite-flat subgroup and quotient constructions with fpqc descent, which overlap the finite-group-scheme torsor quotients of item 2.
Owns the fppf sheaf quotient of a group scheme and its representability under hypotheses, the group case of the torsor quotient of item 2.

targets.target: Finite étale morphisms: sections, fibre cardinalities, local constancy of the degree, cancellation, descent
targets.note: Mathlib has étale cancellation (f ≫ g étale and g unramified of finite type implies f étale), stability under composition and base change, and local constancy of the rank of a finite flat finitely presented morphism. Over a separably closed field a finite étale algebra is a finite product of copies of the field, which gives fibre cardinalities. Not found: a statement that sections of finite étale morphisms are open and closed, or descent of finite étaleness along fppf covers.

targets.target: Over a field K, the equivalence between finite étale K-schemes and finite continuous Gal(Kˢ/K)-sets
targets.note: Only the separably closed case is proved: finite étale Ω-algebras are anti-equivalent to finite sets. The fibre functor at a geometric point and the abstract Galois-category theorem (C ⥤ Action FintypeCat (Aut F) is full and faithful) exist, but finite étale algebras over a general field are not shown to form a Galois category, and Aut of the fibre functor is not identified with Gal(Kˢ/K).

targets.target: The equivalence preserves products and transports group objects, commutative group objects, homomorphisms and alternating pairings
targets.note: Depends on the equivalence above, which is missing; no transport of group objects or pairings exists.

duplicates.note: Constructs the automorphism group of the geometric fibre functor on finite étale covers with its equivalence to finite continuous sets, recovering the absolute Galois group for Spec K: the general form of 0D's equivalence.

targets.target: Effective faithfully flat descent, with cocycle and uniqueness, for affine schemes
targets.note: Mathlib proves that extension of scalars along a faithfully flat ring map is comonadic, and the Amitsur equalizer A = eq(B ⇉ B ⊗_A B), and it has the general IsStack formalism. Its own docstring leaves effective descent for the module pseudofunctor as a TODO, and no stack instance for affine schemes or algebras exists.

targets.target: Descent of sections and morphisms along fppf/fpqc covers
targets.note: Both topologies are proved subcanonical by unnamed instances (Fpqc.lean lines 87 and 97), and quasi-compact flat surjections and fppf surjections are effective epimorphisms (lines 114 and 123). So morphisms and sections descend uniquely along these covers.

targets.target: Effective descent for finite locally free schemes, closed subschemes, finite locally free subgroup schemes and Cartier-divisor equalities
targets.note: Mathlib descends properties of morphisms (isomorphism, open immersion, universally closed and open), not objects. No effective descent of schemes or subschemes exists.

targets.target: Effective descent of projective relative curves equipped with a compatibly descended relatively ample line bundle
targets.note: No relative ampleness or polarised descent exists in either library.

targets.target: Descent of group objects, homomorphisms, the group law and its axioms, level structures, finite group actions and torsors
targets.note: Only Tau Ceti's descent of the group of points of an affine group: A-points are the B-points with equal restrictions to B ⊗_A B. Descent of group-object structures, level structures and torsors is absent.

targets.target: Spreading out: finite-presentation models for a polarised curve with section, group law, subgroup and level data; morphisms and equalities descend to a common finite stage
targets.note: For a cofiltered limit of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps, Mathlib has that morphisms to a locally finitely presented target factor through a finite stage, and that two morphisms agreeing on the limit agree at a finite stage. Missing: descending the objects themselves (curve, polarisation, group law, subgroup, level data) to a finite stage.

targets.target: The agreement locus of two finitely presented morphisms is representable and contains the original base after enlargement
targets.note: Equalizers of scheme morphisms exist, and into a separated target the equalizer is a closed immersion; agreement on the limit propagates to a finite stage. The combined statement is not formulated.

duplicates.note: Builds effective étale descent for schemes with a compatible relatively ample invertible sheaf, with descent of morphisms, sections and the polarisation. This is 0E's polarised-projective case, and it likewise refuses unpolarised effectivity.

Proves effective descent for sheaves, finite flat groups, polarisations and projective objects, keeping descent of a line bundle separate from descent of an object with it. The same object list as 0E.
Owns effective fpqc/fppf descent for the required objects in general.

targets.target: Weil restriction: for Z ⟶ S finite locally free and X ⟶ Z affine of finite presentation, the functor of Z-morphisms is represented by an affine S-scheme
targets.note: Neither tree defines Weil restriction or restriction of scalars for schemes, or any Hom or Isom scheme; a source grep for these names finds nothing.

targets.target: Special cases: tuples of sections of a finite locally free S-scheme; homomorphisms between finite locally free group schemes; ambient schemes for the full-set, exact-order and full-level loci
targets.note: No representability statement for sections or homomorphisms of finite flat group schemes exists. Tau Ceti's affine group-scheme library represents only specific subgroup functors, such as the centre and dynamic parabolics of GLₙ.

targets.target: Compatibility of these representing schemes with arbitrary base change
targets.note: No carrier to state it for.

duplicates.note: Owns restriction of scalars for affine finite-type schemes along a finite locally free base map, by its functor-of-points universal property. That is exactly 0F's general Weil-restriction theorem.
Develops relative Hom and Isom schemes for the moduli proofs that invoke them.

targets.target: Relative Grassmannian of locally free rank-N quotients of the Hopf algebra of G/S: affine charts, transition maps, gluing, representability and universal property
targets.note: As the roadmap says, Mathlib has only the functor A ↦ G(k, A ⊗ M; A) of submodules with locally free rank-k quotient. Its own TODO list names charts, the scheme over a base scheme, and representability as missing.

targets.target: Closed loci cut out by the unit, multiplication, counit, comultiplication, antipode and Hopf-ideal equations
targets.note: Both libraries define a Hopf ideal of a fixed Hopf algebra, but none treats the Hopf-ideal condition as a closed condition on a family of quotients over a parameter scheme.

targets.target: The universal quotient's relative spectrum is a finite locally free rank-N subgroup scheme of G, compatible with base change; the parameter scheme is projective and finitely presented, and need not be finite
targets.note: No parameter space for subgroup schemes exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Constructs Grassmannians with their quotient universal properties and base change, and proves that invariant-subbundle equations are closed. That covers 0G's Grassmannian and closed-loci steps.
Hilbert and Quot schemes realised inside Grassmannians: the general parameter-space theory of which the scheme of rank-N subgroup schemes is a special case.

targets.target: 1A: projective Weierstrass models as proper smooth pointed curves, and EllipticCurveGeom S with its pointed local-Weierstrass atlas
targets.note: No scheme is attached to a Weierstrass equation in either library; only properness of Proj is available as an input. Details under 1A.

targets.target: 1B: the points dictionary over fields, local rings, trivial-Picard rings and arbitrary bases
targets.note: Details under 1B.

targets.target: 1C: pole sheaves π_*𝒪_E(n[0]), the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, the variable-change group and the classification of pointed isomorphisms
targets.note: Only the equation-level variable-change group and its transformation laws exist; the relative cohomology, the presentation theorem and the classification do not. Details under 1C.

targets.target: 1D: the scheme-theoretic group law by charts, and EllipticCurve S
targets.note: Details under 1D.

targets.target: 1E: the cubic polarisation and elliptic descent
targets.note: Details under 1E.

duplicates.note: Identifies one-dimensional abelian schemes with this layer's elliptic curves over a base, using its Weierstrass-presentation theorem.

targets.target: The projective cubic of W : WeierstrassCurve R as a closed subscheme of ℙ²_R, with structure morphism and zero section [0:1:0]
targets.note: Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve.Projective is the equation in homogeneous coordinates, with point classes over a field. Neither library builds a scheme from a Weierstrass equation (mathlib4#25983 is an open PR), and neither has ℙ²_R as a named scheme.

targets.target: Properness of the projective model
targets.note: Mathlib proves Proj 𝒜 ⟶ Spec 𝒜₀ proper for 𝒜 of finite type over 𝒜₀ (an unnamed instance at Proper.lean line 372). Applied to the graded quotient R[X,Y,Z]/(F) this would give properness, but the model is not constructed.

targets.target: Smoothness of relative dimension one when W.IsElliptic
targets.note: Only the equation-level fact: on an elliptic curve over a nontrivial ring every solution of the equation is nonsingular. No scheme smoothness statement exists.

targets.target: Compatibility of the model with base change and with VariableChange
targets.note: Equation level only: the variable-change group acts on Weierstrass curves over any commutative ring, and the action commutes with ring maps. The scheme-level compatibilities are missing with the model.

targets.target: EllipticCurveGeom S: smooth proper π : E ⟶ S of relative dimension one with a section, Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model; base change and its functoriality
targets.note: No elliptic curve over a base scheme exists in either library. The closest carrier is Tau Ceti's AbelianVariety K: a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field, with no Weierstrass atlas and no non-field base.

duplicates.note: Proves that one-dimensional abelian schemes coincide with this roadmap's scheme-theoretic elliptic curves via the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, so it shares the EllipticCurve S carrier and consumes 1A–1D.

targets.target: Over a field with W elliptic, sections of projModel W ⟶ Spec K correspond to W.toAffine.Point, the zero section to infinity
targets.note: Mathlib identifies nonsingular projective point classes with affine points over a field (an equation-level dictionary), but there is no projective model scheme whose sections could be compared.

targets.target: Over a local ring, points as unimodular homogeneous triples; over a ring with trivial Picard group, the same after trivialising the line bundle
targets.note: Mathlib's projective point classes are defined only over fields; no functor-of-points description of projective space over a ring exists.

targets.target: Over an arbitrary base T, T-points as a line bundle with three generating sections satisfying the cubic, up to isomorphism, proved by Zariski descent
targets.note: Mathlib has no functor of points of ℙⁿ, contrary to the layer's stated dependency on 'Mathlib's projective-space functor of points'. Module.Grassmannian.functor exists, but its representability is a TODO.

targets.target: The relative effective Cartier divisor [0], its multiples, and the line bundles ℒ_n = 𝒪_E(n[0])
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs 𝒪_X(D) for a Weil divisor on a noetherian integral scheme of dimension at most one (an absolute curve), not for a divisor on a relative curve over a base.

targets.target: For n > 0: R¹π_*ℒ_n = 0, π_*ℒ_n locally free of rank n, formation commuting with arbitrary base change
targets.note: Only the fibre dimension exists, in function-field language: ℓ(nP) = n at a rational place of a genus-one function field. Tau Ceti also has absolute sheaf cohomology Hⁱ(X, M). No higher direct images, local freeness of pushforwards, or cohomology and base change exist.

targets.target: Positive-degree theorem: for M invertible of constant positive fibre degree d, R¹π_*M = 0, π_*M locally free of rank d with base change; for d = 1 the zero divisor of the evaluation section is a unique section, compatibly with base change and fppf descent
targets.note: Requires the relative cohomology package of the Jacobian Challenge, which is not in either library.

targets.target: Pole-filtration construction of a pointed Weierstrass equation Zariski-locally on the base, with unit discriminant; identification of the bases 1, x, y, x², xy, x³ and of the pole-order-six relation with the Weierstrass equation
targets.note: Not even the field case exists: neither library derives a Weierstrass equation from a genus-one function field with a rational place.

targets.target: The variable-change group x = u²x′ + r, y = u³y′ + su²x′ + t: multiplication, inverse, action on the five coefficients, on x, y and on the invariant differential, and the transformation law of the equation
targets.note: Mathlib has the group (with the action on coefficients and invariance of Δ and j) over any commutative ring. Tau Ceti adds the transformation of the equation and of the group-law formulae over a ring, and the induced isomorphism of point groups over a field. Missing: the transformation law of the invariant differential under a variable change (Tau Ceti's ω lives only in the Kähler differentials of the function field).

targets.target: Classification: every pointed isomorphism of projective Weierstrass models over the same base is induced by a unique variable change, over an arbitrary base by descent
targets.note: Not proved even over a field. Tau Ceti's Aut.lean takes variable changes as the definition of isomorphism of Weierstrass curves rather than proving it, and its degree-one isogenies are not related to variable changes.

targets.target: Weierstrass-presentation theorem: a smooth proper relative genus-one curve with a section is Zariski-locally pointed-isomorphic to a projective Weierstrass model
targets.note: No relative curve theory exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves over a field that an elliptic function field has a Weierstrass equation via the ℓ(iP) = i ladder (Stichtenoth Prop. 6.1.2): the fibrewise case of 1C's pole-filtration construction.

Proves that one-dimensional abelian schemes coincide with this roadmap's scheme-theoretic elliptic curves via the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, so it shares the EllipticCurve S carrier and consumes 1A–1D.

targets.target: Finite chart cover of E ×_S E on which the addition formulae are regular; the formula on each chart; equality on overlaps as scheme morphisms over nonreduced bases
targets.note: Mathlib has the homogeneous addition polynomials as polynomial formulas, and a group law on their nonsingular point classes over a field only. No chart cover, no scheme morphism and no identity of formulae as morphisms exists.

targets.target: Gluing the chart morphisms using the pointed-isomorphism classification, and compatibility with base change
targets.note: Depends on 1C's classification theorem, which is absent.

targets.target: Identity, inverse, associativity, commutativity and inverse laws as scheme morphisms; EllipticCurve S as a commutative group object
targets.note: Mathlib proves that a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative, the input the layer plans to reuse; over a general base it applies only fibrewise. The group law itself is absent.

targets.target: Agreement with Mathlib's pointwise group law on every field-valued fibre
targets.note: The pointwise laws in affine, projective and Jacobian coordinates are identified with each other in Mathlib, but not with any scheme-level law.

duplicates.note: Proves that one-dimensional abelian schemes coincide with this roadmap's scheme-theoretic elliptic curves via the Weierstrass-presentation theorem, so it shares the EllipticCurve S carrier and consumes 1A–1D.

targets.target: 𝒪_T ⟶ (π_T)_*𝒪_{E_T} is an isomorphism for every T ⟶ S, stably under base change
targets.note: No pushforward of structure sheaves along relative curves is studied in either library.

targets.target: 𝒪_E(3[0]) is relatively ample and commutes with arbitrary base change
targets.note: Neither library defines relative ampleness.

targets.target: Descent of an elliptic curve with its polarisation and zero section, then of the group law, finite locally free subgroups, Cartier-divisor equalities and level structures; the same for the universal curve of a rigidifier
targets.note: Depends on the polarised effective descent of 0E, which is absent.

duplicates.note: Builds effective descent for schemes with a relatively ample invertible sheaf and descent of morphisms and sections. That is the general theorem 1E applies to 𝒪_E(3[0]).

targets.target: 2A: Hom_S as group-scheme homomorphisms; [N] finite locally free of rank N² and étale where N is invertible; E[N]; the narrow function-field degree bridge
targets.note: The equation-level input deg [N] = N² (which the roadmap believes its supplier has not exported) and the generic-point extensionality theorem are in the libraries; everything scheme-theoretic is absent. Details under 2A.

targets.target: 2B: quotients E/C by finite locally free subgroups via norms of line bundles, and the factorisation of isogenies through E/ker φ
targets.note: Only the field-level function-field factorisation theorem exists. Details under 2B.

targets.target: 2C: the factorisation dual φ̂_fac
targets.note: No dual isogeny exists at either level. Details under 2C.

targets.target: 2D: relative Picard functor, Poincaré bundle, λ_E : E ≅ Pic⁰, KM 2.5.1, the Picard dual and its comparison with φ̂_fac
targets.note: Details under 2D.

targets.target: 2E: Cartier–Nishi duality and the scheme-theoretic Weil pairing with its eight laws
targets.note: Only the determinant-scaling lemma for alternating forms exists. Details under 2E.

targets.target: 2F: degree and trace of endomorphisms, the characteristic polynomial, and naive-level rigidity
targets.note: Details under 2F.

duplicates.note: Owns the abelian-scheme versions of 2A–2C and 2E: [n] finite locally free of rank n^(2g), fppf quotients, duals and the Weil pairing.
Owns the relative Picard functor and Poincaré bundle for abelian schemes, and is required to recover 2D's elliptic construction.

targets.target: Hom_S(E,E′) as homomorphisms of commutative group schemes over S, End_S(E), and multiplication by an integer in that category
targets.note: The field-base analogue exists: for abelian varieties over a field K, homomorphisms are group-scheme homomorphisms forming a commutative group, End A is a ring, and [n] is its image of n. Missing: the same over an arbitrary base S for elliptic curves, which do not yet exist as objects.

targets.target: [N] : E ⟶ E for N ≠ 0, with base change; nonconstant and quasi-finite on geometric fibres; finite by properness
targets.note: Tau Ceti has [n] as an isogeny of a Weierstrass curve over a field, in the contravariant function-field model; Mathlib has proper + locally quasi-finite ⇒ finite. No scheme morphism [N] over a base exists.

targets.target: The equation-level input deg [N] = N² over a field, consumed from the Elliptic Curves roadmap (pinned in Suggested.lean as EllipticCurvesInterface.mulByIsogeny and degree_mulByIsogeny, described as not yet exported)
targets.note: Proved: for an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a field and n ≠ 0, the function-field degree of [n] is n², including the inseparable case, and its kernel is the n-torsion. The roadmap says the supplier does not yet export [N] as an isogeny or its degree; Tau Ceti already has both at the pin, so the interface pins can be replaced.

targets.target: The narrow function-field bridge: K(projModel W) ≃ W.toAffine.FunctionField, comparison of the scheme and equation-level pullbacks of [N], and generic degree N²; geometric integrality of the smooth cubic
targets.note: No projective model scheme exists to compare with, so none of projModelFunctionFieldEquiv, mulByHom_functionField_eq or mulByHom_genericDegree can be stated.

targets.target: Separated-target extensionality: two morphisms from an integral scheme to a separated target that agree at the generic point agree everywhere
